kill_fact: The catalyst itself survives primary-source checking - the 30 September 2026 PDUFA action date for apitegromab is live, hard-dated and binding, restated by the company in its own 20 July 2026 release, and the spread has widened rather than closed ($47.67 close on 24 July 2026, down from $56.71 on 10 July). What does NOT survive is the single load-bearing claim the bull case is built on: that 'the American decision is not gated on Catalent'. No primary source says that, and the company's own Form 10-Q says the opposite in plain terms: 'The Company resubmitted the apitegromab BLA in March 2026 with two fill-finish facilities included, which was accepted by the Agency with a September 30, 2026 PDUFA action date.' BOTH sites are inside the accepted U.S. application. Nothing on the disclosed record removes Catalent Indiana from the U.S. filing. Worse, the dossier's characterisation of the Catalent problem is materially incomplete: its dated evidence chain stops at a Form 483 (14 July 2025) and an Official Action Indicated classification, and calls the CRL 'the most fixable category of regulatory refusal that exists' arising from 'a routine general site inspection'. It never mentions that the FDA escalated to a formal Warning Letter (320-26-20, issued 20 November 2025) - an enforcement action Scholar Rock discloses in its own 10-Q, which references a third-party fill-finish facility that received a Form 483 with an OAI classification 'and subsequently a Warning Letter'. The cited violations are sterility-assurance failures in the exact operation apitegromab depends on: more than twenty inadequately investigated deviations involving mammalian hair contamination in or around the stopper region of vials, and more than five terminated media fill batches since November 2023. A site under an unresolved Warning Letter is a routine bar to approval of any application that names it, and closing one out requires FDA to accept documented remediation - a far higher bar than the bureaucratic slowness the dossier implies when it calls the classification merely 'overdue'. The European regulator is visibly applying exactly this logic to the MAA. The bull calls the sell-off a 'category error' by investors who confused Europe with America; on the disclosed record it is at least as likely that the market is pricing the same unresolved, Warning-Lettered site that sits in BOTH filings. The 78% approval weight, the $57 probability-weighted base case and the entire timing argument rest on an inference the company has never made in its own words and on a severity framing the company's own filings contradict. Two further load-bearing numbers are wrong in the bull's favour: (1) the sum-of-the-parts divides by 119.8m shares, but Q1 2026 weighted-average shares - basic AND diluted - were 127,277,144, so every per-share figure is flattered by roughly 6% and enterprise value is ~$5.8bn not $5.44bn, i.e. ~3.9x consensus peak sales rather than 3.6x; and (2) the $150m approval-contingent tranche is an UNCOMMITTED incremental facility subject to customary conditions including a minimum cash covenant - weaker than the dossier's 'committed capital' framing, which makes the failure case worse, not better. Finally, the $28 floor is calibrated on the wrong experiment. The October 2025 clearing price of $27.07 was set by a market that believed a first, contractor-specific refusal was quickly fixable. A SECOND manufacturing refusal - after a second qualified site was written into the filing precisely to prevent it - destroys that belief and is a categorically worse signal, from a higher starting price ($47.67 vs $39.46) and a materially larger cost base. Using the first-CRL trade as the 'verified floor' for the second-CRL scenario is directionally optimistic, and the board's $14 is not the sub-5% tail the dossier assigns it. There is no contractual backstop of any kind: net cash is ~$2.2-2.4 per share against a $47.67 stock, so ~95% of the price is a claim on one regulatory decision.
corrections: 1) CATALYST INDEPENDENCE - REFUTED AS STATED, MATERIAL. Delete the assertion that the U.S. date is insulated from Catalent. The Q1 2026 Form 10-Q states the BLA was resubmitted 'with two fill-finish facilities included' and accepted with the 30 September 2026 PDUFA date; the 7 May 2026 release likewise describes an accepted BLA containing Catalent Indiana AND the second U.S. site. No disclosure removes Catalent from the U.S. filing. Correct framing: the second site is a credible remedy, but whether the FDA will sign a BLA that still names a Warning-Lettered, OAI-classified facility is undisclosed and unknowable from outside. The consensus_delta section must be rewritten - 'investors sold an American catalyst on European news' is not established; the market may be pricing a shared, unresolved manufacturing input. 2) WARNING LETTER OMITTED - MATERIAL, NEW. The dated evidence chain must add: FDA Warning Letter 320-26-20 issued to Catalent Indiana, LLC on 20 November 2025, following the 23 June - 14 July 2025 inspection of the Bloomington, Indiana site, citing CGMP violations under 21 CFR 210/211 including more than twenty inadequately investigated deviations involving mammalian hair contamination in or around the vial stopper region and more than five terminated media fill batches since November 2023. Scholar Rock discloses this escalation in its own 10-Q. The dossier's phrases 'routine general site inspection', 'not specific to apitegromab', 'nothing was wrong with the medicine' and 'the most fixable category of regulatory refusal that exists' are therefore materially understated: this is an open sterility-assurance enforcement action against the primary fill-finish site, not a paperwork observation. This is the correction that most damages the 78% weight, because that weight was explicitly calibrated on the 'nothing was wrong, routine inspection' framing. 3) PROBABILITY WEIGHTS - the 78/15/7 split is downstream of corrections (1) and (2) and should be widened materially in favour of the extension and second-refusal branches until the Catalent classification lands or the 6 August 2026 call clarifies both the classification and whether a pre-approval inspection of the second site is outstanding. 4) SHARE COUNT - MATERIAL. Q1 2026 weighted-average shares (basic and diluted) were 127,277,144, not 119.8m; 119,103,774 common shares were outstanding at 31 March 2026 and 119,828,338 at 4 May 2026, the difference to the weighted average being pre-funded warrants that are economically live. Restate the SoP per-share values ~6% lower ($63 event-win becomes ~$59; $28 floor becomes ~$26) and the EV at ~$5.8bn / ~3.9x peak sales. 5) FLOOR METHODOLOGY - MATERIAL. The $28 is not 'verified'; it is an estimate anchored to a non-analogous prior event. Label it as such, widen the range to roughly $20-28, and raise the probability mass on the $14 board floor above the stated sub-5%. 6) FINANCING - the $150m tranche is UNCOMMITTED, available only 'from the date of FDA approval for apitegromab in SMA until the date that is the earliest of the full usage thereof, termination thereof and September 30, 2027', subject to conditions including a minimum cash covenant. Remove 'committed capital' language. 7) DEBT FIGURE - long-term debt carrying value was $196.6m at 31 March 2026, not $205.7m; net cash is therefore ~$283m (~$2.2-2.4/share depending on share count). 8) PEAK SALES - the $1.4-1.5bn base is defensible but the street spans $1-2bn; the SoP's 3.5x-peak-sales present-value multiple is an unsourced heuristic doing most of the work in the $40-46/share SMA block. 9) CONFIRMED AS STATED - the 30 September 2026 PDUFA action date, the 31 March 2026 resubmission accepted by the FDA, the CRL of 22 September 2025 attributed solely to Catalent Indiana observations, the April 2026 Catalent re-inspection with classification anticipated within 90 days and still unannounced as of 20 July 2026, the second site described as U.S.-based and in good standing with FDA and EMA, cash and marketable securities of $479.9m at 31 March 2026 ($430.5m cash plus $49.4m securities), the $47.67 close on 24 July 2026, no going-concern doubt, the 6 August 2026 second-quarter call as the next dated checkpoint, and the EMBRAZE Phase 2 result (+4.2 lbs lean mass, 54.9% preservation, p=0.001, n=102, published in Nature Medicine). Minor footnote on EMBRAZE the dossier omits: total body-weight loss was LOWER on the combination (12.3% vs 13.4%), so the obesity option is a body-composition claim, not a weight-loss-potency claim.
evidence: Scholar Rock Form 10-Q for the quarter ended 31 March 2026 (filed May 2026, CIK 0001727196): 'The Company resubmitted the apitegromab BLA in March 2026 with two fill-finish facilities included, which was accepted by the Agency with a September 30, 2026 PDUFA action date.' The same filing describes the third-party fill-finish facility as having received a Form 483 with an 'official action indicated' classification 'and subsequently a Warning Letter'. Also: 119,103,774 common shares outstanding at 31 March 2026; 127,277,144 weighted-average shares basic and diluted for Q1 2026; long-term debt carrying value $196.6 million; cash and equivalents $430.5 million plus marketable securities $49.4 million; the additional $150.0 million delayed draw term loan commitment 'will be available from the date of FDA approval for apitegromab in SMA until the date that is the earliest of the full usage thereof, termination thereof and September 30, 2027', uncommitted and subject to customary conditions including a minimum cash covenant; no going-concern language. This single filing establishes that BOTH fill-finish sites sit inside the accepted U.S. application and that the primary site carries a Warning Letter.

FDA Warning Letter 320-26-20 issued to Catalent Indiana, LLC (FEI/reference 718189) on 20 November 2025, following the FDA inspection of the sterile fill-finish site at 1300 South Patterson Drive, Bloomington, Indiana conducted 23 June - 14 July 2025. Cites significant CGMP violations under 21 CFR Parts 210 and 211, including failure to adequately investigate more than twenty deviations involving possible mammalian hair contamination in or around the stopper region of vials, investigations not extended to potentially affected product, inadequate CAPA evaluation, and more than five terminated media fill batches since November 2023. Published in the FDA warning-letter database. Omitted entirely from the dossier's dated evidence chain, which stops at the Form 483 and the OAI classification.

Scholar Rock press release, 20 July 2026 - 'Scholar Rock Provides Update on Timing of CHMP Opinion for Apitegromab MAA for SMA': the EMA is 'awaiting an update on the inspection classification of Catalent Indiana from the FDA following an April 2026 general site inspection'; 'Should the FDA reclassify Catalent Indiana, a CHMP opinion would be expected later in 2026'; 'In the event that Catalent Indiana is not reclassified, Scholar Rock will work with the EMA to advance the apitegromab MAA with the Company's second fill-finish facility', which is 'included in the apitegromab Biologics License Application (BLA) under FDA review in the U.S. with a September 30, 2026 Prescription Drug User Fee Act (PDUFA) action date'; the second site 'is a U.S.-based facility producing numerous commercial products and is in good standing with both the FDA and EMA'; 'The Company will provide an update during its second quarter earnings call on Thursday, August 6, 2026.' The release nowhere states that Catalent Indiana has been removed from the U.S. BLA or that the U.S. action date is independent of its classification.

Scholar Rock first-quarter 2026 results, 7 May 2026 (Form 8-K exhibit 99.1, accession 0001104659-26-056655): the accepted apitegromab BLA includes two fill-finish facilities, Catalent Indiana LLC (part of Novo Nordisk) and a second U.S.-based facility; the FDA 'completed reinspection of Catalent Indiana' in April 2026 with 'classification of the facility ... anticipated within 90 days' - a window that had elapsed with no announcement as of the 20 July 2026 release; second-site commercial supply expected 'in early Q3 2026'; PDUFA action date 30 September 2026; cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities of $479.9 million at 31 March 2026, up from $367.6 million at 31 December 2025; net loss $105.5 million and loss per share $(0.83), which reconciles only at ~127 million shares. Management stated on the call that the FDA 'has up to 90 days to classify the facility' and disclosed no pre-approval inspection status for the second site.
